The '''2018–19 Süper Lig''', officially called the '''Spor Toto Süper Lig Lefter Küçükandonyadis season''', was the 61st season of the [[Süper Lig]], the highest tier [[Association football|football]] league of [[Turkey]]. The season began on 10 August 2018 and concluded on 26 May 2019.

The season was named after [[Lefter Küçükandonyadis]], a former Turkey national team player and [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]] legend.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=285&ftxtID=29576|title=Spor Toto Süper Lig'de Lefter Küçükandonyadis sezonu|website=tff.org|publisher=[[Turkish Football Federation]]|access-date=3 August 2018|language=tr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180715235619/http://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=285&ftxtID=29576|archive-date=2018-07-15|url-status=live}}</ref>

This season the [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] was introduced in all games of Süper Lig competition.

==Teams==
A total of 18 teams contest the league, including 15 sides from the [[2017–18 Süper Lig|2017–18 season]] and three promoted from the [[2017–18 TFF First League]]. It includes [[Çaykur Rizespor|Rizespor]] and [[MKE Ankaragücü|Ankaragücü]], the two top teams from the [[TFF First League]], and [[Büyükşehir Belediye Erzurumspor|Erzurum BB]], the winners of the [[2017–18 TFF First League#Promotion Playoffs|2017–18 TFF First League playoffs]].
[[Gençlerbirliği S.K.|Gençlerbirliği]], [[Osmanlıspor]], and [[Kardemir Karabükspor|Karabükspor]] were relegated to [[2018–19 TFF First League]].
